question: Why did same-class overlapping boxes52351/52356 survive the detector when the cache metadata saysIoU0.7?
hypothesis: The frozen detector uses a final-output branch without overlap suppression; metadata records the passed argument but not whether it is applied.
method: Load exact trusted local checkpoint on CPU for metadata only. Record serialized head mode and one-to-one submodules. Inspect original extraction function recovered by SHA256, predictor dispatch and postprocessor branch. Apply only the existing postprocessor to saved final boxes; compare with explicit class-aware greedy suppression at the SAME0.7 as an offline mechanism control. Check whole saved frame and literal IDs, not only selected two boxes.
acceptance: Exact checkpoint/cache/extraction provenance verified; absent historical vendor fingerprints disclosed.
No model forward, no tracker, no core, no threshold change. Original saved arrays remain byte-identical.
Observed output route and independent geometry distinguish no suppression from suppression at the unchanged metadata threshold; do not claim full-tracker improvement.
limits: Current vendor source fingerprints cannot be assigned retroactively to the old process. Loading the checkpoint exposes stored model structure; no historical raw pre-postprocessing tensor was saved. A diagnostic output mask is not a rerun of downstream trajectories.
